title: Auric Tech - Renewal & Regional On-call Planning
summary: Renewal check-in focused on contract extension options, planned capacity uplift for Q4, EU on-prem pilot timeline, and clarifying security/audit requirements. Action items include pricing refresh, pilot SOW draft, and infra benchmark request.
next_steps: Redwood to send revised pricing/term options by 2025-07-25
SE to run latency/cost bench on Aurora-64 profile and share results by 2025-07-29
Draft SOW for EU on-prem pilot to be shared 2025-08-01
Customer to confirm stakeholder list for legal review by 2025-07-24
action_items: Priya Malhotra - produce Aurora-64 latency/cost spreadsheet - due 2025-07-29
Liam Chen - update renewal pricing & term card and send to Sonia - due 2025-07-25
Owen Park - draft EU on-prem pilot SOW and onboarding checklist - due 2025-08-01
Jordan Miles - send finalized list of internal stakeholders + data residency constraints - due 2025-07-24
transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (SE), Owen Park (CSM), Jordan Miles (Auric Head of Platform), Aisha Raza (Infra), Marco DeLeon (CISO), Sonia Patel (Procurement)

[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, we'll keep this tight — main goal is renewal options and the EU on-prem pilot timeline.
[00:18] Jordan Miles: Yeah thanks Liam, quick context, we've been on Redwood for 11 months, currently hosted API with a small dedicated pool for peak traffic. We're hitting token caps in Q4 projections and need a plan for capacity and region expansion.
[00:35] Aisha Raza: And just to add, latency is getting jittery for EU customers, so we're looking at adding EU capacity — open to either Redwood Dedicated in eu-west or an on-prem pilot.
[00:48] Priya Malhotra: Got it. On the Dedicated side we can do reserved GPU pools and burst capacity; for on-prem we have the Private deployment package — VPC + private control plane. Both support pinning model versions and rollout policies.
[01:03] Marco DeLeon: Security first — we need SOC2 + ISO cert copies, audit logs ingestion pattern, KMS/HSM compatibility, and proof that the private control plane can be run behind our firewall.
[01:20] Owen Park: We'll send SOC2 and the compliance pack after this call, and note the Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS. There's a short checklist for network requirements.
[01:34] Sonia Patel: From procurement: we need term options. We prefer a 12–18 month commitment but want an option to add incremental capacity mid-term without reneging on pricing. Also need payment terms.
[01:48] Liam Chen: Understood. Two paths: 1) Reserved Dedicated with an uplift commit for Q4 plus regional eu-west activation; 2) Pilot a small on-prem cluster (EU datacenter) for 3 months, then move to full Private if it meets throughput SLA. Pricing differs — Dedicated is simpler to commit to quickly, on-prem has one-time setup and recurring platform fee.
[02:10] Jordan Miles: Budget leans toward Dedicated but security may push us to on-prem. Can you provide TCO comparison? Latency vs cost tradeoff is key.
[02:23] Priya Malhotra: We can run a controlled benchmark: we'll replicate a typical Auric production workload (20% chat, 60% short generation, 20% embeddings) and measure p95 latency, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens on Aurora-64 and Aurora-32 quantized variants. That should show delta between Dedicated in eu-west and a small on-prem footprint.
[02:45] Aisha Raza: That would help. Also we need to understand KV cache implications for multi-tenant workloads — will caching be shared across requests? How does that impact our latency for contextual retrieval?
[02:59] Priya Malhotra: Caching is prefix/KV cache per customer and per model version. For Dedicated it's managed, for Private you control the cache nodes. There can be warmup strategies to avoid cold-start latencies.
[03:14] Marco DeLeon: Encryption at rest and in transit details — we run keys in an HSM, we need Redwood to confirm KMS integration and that logs can be pushed to our SIEM. Also need SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping for teams.
[03:30] Owen Park: We support KMS integrations with AWS KMS and a customer HSM gateway; logs can stream to your SIEM via secure delivery. We documented SSO mapping in the enterprise onboarding guide; we'll include a sample mapping.
[03:44] Jordan Miles: Timeline question: if we wanted EU capacity in time for our Black Friday-type promo in Nov, what's realistic?
[03:53] Priya Malhotra: If you go Dedicated eu-west: provisioning + testing is about 3–4 weeks from PO. For Private on-prem, plan ~8–12 weeks given site access, network setup, and the pilot SOW. Pilot can be compressed with pre-staging but still more ops.
[04:11] Sonia Patel: So Dedicated is faster and cheaper initially. Procurement wants a few variable pricing slots so we can burst without renegotiating.
[04:20] Liam Chen: We can include burst credits in the contract and a tiered pricing table for incremental capacity. We'll draft two term cards: a 12-month committed Dedicated plan with optional burst pool, and an 18-month plan with a discounted on-prem transition credit if you move to Private after pilot.
[04:39] Aisha Raza: About SLAs — p95 response target and uptime. We need clarity on degraded mode fallback; if the EU region is constrained, can requests route to another region automatically while still meeting data residency?
[04:55] Priya Malhotra: Smart routing can route by policy — latency-first or cost-first — and for data residency you can set region constraints so fallback won't cross residency boundaries. For strict residency you'd want Private or Dedicated in-region to avoid cross-border routing.
[05:14] Marco DeLeon: We also need to know retention — logs, request/response data retention and whether we can disable storing customer data for hosted inference.
[05:24] Owen Park: We offer configurable retention; for Private, data never leaves your network. For Hosted/ Dedicated, you can opt-out of storing request payloads and we can set retention windows. We'll include the retention policy matrix.
[05:36] Jordan Miles: Ok can we talk numbers? If we bump from current 4x capacity to 10x in Q4, what's the incremental monthly?
[05:45] Liam Chen: Roughly speaking, for the Aurora-64 profile you're looking at an X3 multiplier vs base hosted due to GPU sizing and throughput. I'll send a modeled TCO that includes preferred quantization (Aurora-32) which can reduce token cost by ~30% for non-LLM-critical calls. We'll attach the model mix assumptions.
[06:06] Sonia Patel: Procurement will want a carve-out: if we exceed committed units by more than 20% consistently, how are overages billed?
[06:15] Liam Chen: Overages billed at the burst rate, and we can define a smoothing clause or auto-scale thresholds with alerts to avoid surprises. We'll include an overage cap option in one of the term cards.
[06:28] Aisha Raza: For the on-prem pilot, what orchestration is required from our ops? Do you provide an installer or an image?
[06:37] Priya Malhotra: We provide an on-prem package (container images + orchestration docs), a private control plane, and a hands-on onboarding service. For air-gapped environments there's an extra packaging step. We'll outline network ports, NTP, and certificate rotation requirements in the SOW.
[06:53] Marco DeLeon: Good. Also want to see the audit trail layout — what fields are captured and how long they're stored by default.
[07:02] Owen Park: We'll include an audit sample and retention options; default is 90 days for verbose logs, configurable to your policy.
[07:10] Jordan Miles: Sounds good. Let's make sure the benchmarks mirror our production mix, not synthetic tiny loads.
[07:18] Priya Malhotra: Agreed. We'll need a sample of your workload patterns and a few API keys to run end-to-end test harness.
[07:27] Jordan Miles: Who will lead the pilot on Redwood side?
[07:30] Liam Chen: Priya will lead the bench and pilot technical work; Owen will own onboarding and SOW; I'll handle pricing and contract terms.
[07:39] Sonia Patel: We'll want a single doc summarizing pricing, SOW, and security pack for the legal team.
[07:45] Liam Chen: We'll send one consolidated packet.
[07:49] 
[07:50] -- 20 minute silence of note -- (transcript jumps) 
[08:10] Priya Malhotra: Quick note on KV cache semantics for retrieval-heavy calls — if you plan many short-context calls, quantization and prefix caching will greatly reduce cost per token. We'll show two config suggestions in the bench results.
[08:28] Jordan Miles: Excellent. Anything else?
[08:32] Marco DeLeon: One more security ask: red-team/pen test window for the pilot — can we schedule a time to run internal scans once the pilot cluster is up?
[08:41] Owen Park: Yes, we'll include a pen test window and rules of engagement in the SOW.
[08:46] Liam Chen: Great. Recap: Redwood to send pricing cards and term options by 2025-07-25; SE to run benchmarks and share by 2025-07-29; SOW draft for an EU on-prem pilot by 2025-08-01. Customer to confirm stakeholder list by 2025-07-24.
[09:03] Jordan Miles: That timeline works, thanks all.
[09:07] Liam Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet.
[09:12] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: Some speaker overlaps and minor transcription errors (product names sometimes as Aurora vs Aurora-64). Occasional run-ons and filler words preserved.
